core_obligations: Forward direction (proof lines 2829-2868): F quasi-coherent gives F_n quasi-coherent by the pullback lemma; for cartesianness, take U in C_n, choose a presentation of F over a covering {U_i -> U} of C_total (which is a C_n-covering by construction); for any V in C_m over varphi : [n] -> [m], the fibre products V_i = V x_U U_i give a covering {V_i -> V} of C_m, the presentation restricts to C_n/U_i and C_m/V_i, and the restriction maps defining F(varphi) : f_varphi^*F_n -> F_m make the restricted presentations compatible, so F(varphi)|_{C_m/V_i} is an isomorphism on the covering, hence F(varphi)|_{C_m/V} is an isomorphism (case A via the Sites covering lemma); U and V arbitrary, so F is cartesian.

Converse direction (lines 2870-2892): F cartesian and all F_n quasi-coherent - choose presentations over C_n-coverings and pull them back to C_total/U_i; cartesianness implies the pulled-back presentation complex is exact (the author marks this verification 'we omit the details' - see notes), giving a presentation of F, so F is quasi-coherent.
proof_roadmap: Forward: pull presentations along component morphisms and use the covering {V_i -> V} to promote pointwise isomorphisms to cartesianness.
Converse: pull component presentations back to the total site and invoke cartesianness for exactness.
difficulty_reason: Characterization lemma (statement 2816-2825, proof 2827-2892): the forward direction is a complete presentation-restriction argument promoting isomorphisms on coverings to cartesianness; the converse direction constructs the total-site presentation in full and ends with a short exactness verification marked 'we omit the details' (recorded in the notes). H2: hands-on sheaf-of-modules argument over the total site.
